extracted.intended_audience: law students, practitioners, and general readers interested in United States patent law
extracted.subtask_description: Explain the role and types of transitional phrases that link a patent claim preamble to the claim elements and how each type affects claim scope and infringement analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional phrase (definition and role)
rubrics_metrics.description: A transitional phrase, in United States patent law, is a phrase that links the preamble of a patent claim to the specific elements set forth in the claim which define what the invention itself actually is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transitional phrase acts as a limitation on the claim, indicating whether a similar device, method, or composition infringes the patent if it contains more or fewer elements than the claim in the patent. The article notes there are three kinds of transitional phrases: open, closed, and hybrid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed transition ("consisting of")
rubrics_metrics.description: A closed transition usually uses the words "consisting of." Use of this phrase limits the preamble to exactly what follows and nothing more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a claim for a pencil with the closed transition "consisting of" followed by a cylinder of writing material and a casing means a third party who adds an eraser would not be infringing. Use of a closed transition makes it easier for competitors to design around the claim (they may add elements and avoid infringement), but it may help the patent owner avoid prior art that would otherwise block the patent from issuing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open transition ("comprises" or "comprising")
rubrics_metrics.description: An open transition usually uses the word "comprises" or "comprising." This is the broadest form of transition, as it does not limit the preamble to whatever elements are identified in the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if the pencil claim used "comprising" instead of "consisting of," the pencil-plus-eraser would be infringing (assuming validity). Open transitions broaden claim scope and make it easier to capture products or methods that include additional, unrecited elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid transition ("consisting essentially of")
rubrics_metrics.description: A hybrid transition uses the phrase "consisting essentially of." The effect is to leave the claim open to include additional elements, but only if those additional elements do not materially affect the basic and novel characteristics of the claimed combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a pencil with an added eraser might still not infringe, but additions that are non-material to claimed functions (e.g., a fin or non-functional button) would still infringe. This phrasing can help avoid prior art while remaining broad enough to capture imperfect attempts to copy the patented device.
